Give Me Liberty Street Party

  • Thursday, September 17, 2026
  • 4:00 p.m. 11:00 p.m.
  • Google Calendar ICS

Liberty Village’s Signature Annual After-Work-Street Party

Get ready for an unforgettable celebration of community, creativity, and culture!

🎉On Thursday, September 17th, 2026, the iconic Lamport Stadium parking lot (75 Fraser Avenue) will transform into a dynamic outdoor festival for the Give Me Liberty street party. This one-night-only event is the Liberty Village BIA’s signature celebration, showcasing the vibrant spirit and unique character of our community.

✨What to Expect:

  • Over 40 Local Vendors: Shop, explore, and support Liberty Village businesses.

  • Live Music & Entertainment: Groove to amazing performances from talented artists.

  • Interactive Activities: Dive into fun, engaging experiences for all ages.

Whether you’re here to discover local talent, network with fellow community members, or simply enjoy the ultimate after-work party, Give Me Liberty has something for everyone.

📍Location: Lamport Stadium Parking Lot, 75 Fraser Avenue
🗓️Date: Thursday, September 17th, 2026
⏰ Time: 4:00 PM – 11:00 PM.

Book your free tickets here!

This celebration truly brings together the best of Liberty Village in one extraordinary experience. Don’t miss out!

Canadian National Exhibition

  • Fri, Aug 15, 2025 10:00 a.m. Mon, Sep 1, 2025 10:00 p.m.
  • Google Calendar ICS

The Canadian National Exhibition (CNE) is Canada’s largest community event and one of the top agricultural fairs in North America. Founded in 1879 as the Toronto Industrial Exhibition, the CNE is a not-for-profit organization that has enjoyed a distinguished history as a showcase of the nation. Although the CNE has changed significantly over the years, it continues to be one of Ontario’s great annual traditions and an event that offers substantial entertainment.

Caribbean Carnival

  • Saturday, August 2, 2025
  • 8:00 a.m. 8:00 p.m.
  • Google Calendar ICS

Since 1967, North America's biggest Caribbean Carnival happens in Toronto every year!

The road becomes the stage for the masqueraders and steelpan performers. It truly is something you can’t miss. Toronto Caribbean Carnival's Grande Parade continues to attract local, regional, national, and international attention by visitors and media as it is the highlight of the three-week Festival. This event continues to draw millions from all over the world to see the live performing street art year after year and on live streaming.

The Ontario Honda Dealers Indy Toronto is an annual Indy Car race, held in Toronto. The track is constructed throughout and around Exhibition Place grounds and utilizes Lake Shore Boulevard.

Getting Around

    • Streetcars: Take the 504 King Streetcar (and its branches 504A/504B) to Liberty Village. TTC website

    • Subway: Take the 1 (Yonge-University) or 2 (Bloor-Danforth) subway lines. Transfer to St. Andrew or King stations to reach Liberty Village. TTC Subway Info

    Bus Routes: The 29 Dufferin, 63 Ossington and 929 express buses serve the area. Bus Info

  • Exhibition Station: Take the GO Train to the Exhibition Station. It’s a short walk from there to Liberty Village.

    • The UP Express connects Pearson Airport to Union Station. Once at Union Station, transfer to the 504 King Streetcar to Liberty Village.

    Travel time: Approximately 25-30 minutes. UP Express website

    • By Taxi/Car: Head east on Airport Road and take Dixon Road to the 401 Expressway East. Exit at Dufferin Street or Strachan Avenue to Liberty Village.

    • By Transit: Take the UP Express (Union Pearson Express) from Pearson Airport to Union Station, then transfer to the 504 King Streetcar to Liberty Village.

    • Travel time: Approximately 35-45 minutes by car. Pearson Airport Directions

    From Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (Porter):

    • By Ferry: Take the Porter Ferry from Billy Bishop Airport to the mainland. Walk to King Street and catch the 504 King Streetcar to Liberty Village.

    • By Taxi/Car: Drive east along Queens Quay West towards Spadina Avenue, then turn south onto King Street and head west to Liberty Village.

    • Travel time: About 15-20 minutes by taxi. Porter Airport Directions

  • Find nearby parking at Parkopedia or via our Google Parking Map.

  • Visit the link to find all the bike-share station locations.

Thank you!

Liberty Village is on Indigenous land. This is the traditional territory of the Haudenosaunee Confederacy (aka. the Six Nations Confederacy), the Wendat, and the Mississaugas of the Credit First Nation. Liberty Village BIA gratefully acknowledges these Indigenous nations for their guardianship of this land. We’d also like to remind and reaffirm, as Torontonians and Canadians, our accountability to these Indigenous nations, and to all Indigenous peoples and communities living in Toronto.

This land is also part of the Dish with One Spoon territory, a treaty between the Haudenosaunee Confederacy (aka. The Six Nations Confederacy), the Anishinaabek and allied nations, to peaceably share and care for this land, its waters, and all of the biodiversity in the Great Lakes region. All those who come to live and work here are responsible for honouring this treaty in the spirit of peace, friendship, and respect.
